# ML-KEM-1024 test vectors for test_framework/crypto/mlkem.py. A small subset of the sources below;
# each record is one line: a kind, then space-separated name=value fields, hex in lowercase.
#
# keyGen, encapsulation, decapsulation: NIST ACVP-Server (https://github.com/usnistgov/ACVP-Server),
#   commit 975de31eb83d87039ec88934fdc47d8c312b892d, gen-val/json-files/ML-KEM-keyGen-FIPS203/internalProjection.json
#   (tgId 3, ML-KEM-1024, tcId 51, 52) and
#   gen-val/json-files/ML-KEM-encapDecap-FIPS203/internalProjection.json (tgId 3 encapsulation,
#   tcId 51, 52; tgId 6 decapsulation, tcId 96, 97, 98; tgId 12
#   encapsulationKeyCheck, tcId 156, 159, 160, 161, 163). Field names follow ACVP: c is the ciphertext
#   and k the shared secret; a decapsulation with reason=modified_ciphertext expects the
#   implicit-rejection secret; an encapsulationKeyCheck with passed=0 is an ek that must fail the
#   FIPS 203 section 7.2 check.
#
# modulus: C2SP CCTV (https://github.com/C2SP/CCTV/tree/main/ML-KEM), commit
#   50a8ecf2a220f4c8bdc4f085789b8e85c26829e7, ML-KEM/modulus/ML-KEM-1024.txt.gz: encapsulation keys that each
#   carry one coefficient in [q, 4095] and must fail the FIPS 203 modulus check. line is the line
#   number in that file: lines 1-16 (q and 4095 at the first and last coefficient of each
#   polynomial) and every 64th line from line 18. The keys share all other coefficients, so line 1 is
#   stored in full and the others as byte patches against it (patch=offset:hex,...); sha256 is the
#   SHA-256 of the line's key bytes in the source file, which the tests check after patching.
